articles.title: Sacha Baron Cohen Says Donald Trump Has ‘Elements of Brilliance’ and ‘We Were Too Easy to Dismiss Him as a Nincompoop’
articles.summary: 20 years after retiring Ali G, Sacha Baron Cohen has dusted off his tracksuit collection and reprised the character for “Ali G: Who Iz I?,” now open in theaters before coming to Amazon Prime Oct. 30. The comedian first brought Ali G to audiences at the turn of the century with “Da Ali G Show,”
body: “Later on, I heard that he used to do that with other people,” Baron Cohen said. “It really was a power move.”

Trump appeared taken with Bobin, who Baron Cohen described as a “very handsome, blond, Oxford-educated” Englishman. But when he realized he’d be sitting down with Ali G instead, his demeanor “immediately” changed.

“I actually met a woman who was in the car with him after that interview, and he was apparently furious,” Baron Cohen said. “He actually went out publicly a couple of times to criticize me. And in the end, we used all those clips and used them to advertise another show that I did.”

Baron Cohen’s interview with Trump aired in 2003, back when the future president was best known as a New York real estate mogul, before going on to host NBC’s “The Apprentice.” Looking back at their encounter, Baron Cohen said he could understand how Trump won a second term in the White House, pointing to the president’s “elements of brilliance.”

articles.title: Why Olivia Colman Didn’t Get Splinters From Getting Intimate With Alexander Skarsgård’s ‘Wicker’ Costume
articles.summary: Believe the hype. “Wicker,” now in theaters, is every bit as horny, romantic and wonderful as the trailer leads you to believe. Olivia Colman plays a spinster fisherwoman in a medieval community where marriage is what gives a woman worth.
body: It began with Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson, who were adapting Ursula Wills’ short story “The Wicker Husband.” Weta Workshop artists, prosthetic makeup designer Joe Dunckley and lead makeup FX artist Sarah Rubano received the script and a call from the writers and directors who told them, “We want to make this practically,” says Dunckley. “They wanted a piece of beautiful concept art that showed their vision.”

The pair spent 18 months in research and development alone. Because prosthetic makeup materials are manufactured to imitate human flesh and skin, it posed a challenge. “This guy is made of wicker, so we had to do it a different way,” Dunckley says. He continues, “We tested our theory. We thought that if we could get the strands of the weave to be individual and get them to move as if they were individual muscle fibers that drove his movement, then he could be a believable sentient wicker being.”
But they couldn’t mold it, so the pair were pushed toward modern innovation using 3D digital sculpting and 3D printing.
They began with a full-body scan of Skarsgård so they could sculpt pieces specific to him.

articles.title: I expect you to cry: what the James Bond actors may face at the final audition
articles.summary: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor are rumoured to be the final candidates taking screentests this weekend. So how can they best prepare? And who is likely to triumph? This weekend, the identity of the next James Bond is finally expected to be known – to the insiders, at least.
body: To say it has been a long time coming is an understatement. It is five years since Daniel Craig was killed in a hail of missiles at the end of No Time to Die, and in that time – even long before it – a swarm of actors have been tipped to replace him, only to age out of the role due to a combination of indecisiveness and cutthroat backstage corporate shenanigans. Whoever is declared to be 007 will be joining the franchise after what is likely to be the longest fallow period in the franchise’s 64-year history.
As such, this is kind of a big weekend. Let’s run through what we know so far.

If three actors are to screen test for Bond this weekend, then they are Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden. If there are more – some outlets state that one other actor might be participating, others two – then they won’t include Jack O’Connell or Jacob Elordi, who are both out of the race for one reason or another.

The identity of the other actors are not yet known. Let’s take an uneducated guess and assume that one of them is a Beatle (the best fit is Harris Dickinson) and another one is more famous but less suitable (like Tom Cruise).
points: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor are rumoured to be the final candidates taking screentests this weekend.

articles.title: ‘Fighting an impossible fight is the only way to reclaim dignity’: Lee Chang-dong on class warfare and his searing Oscar contender
articles.summary: The auteur’s new film – a study of labour, capital and the fallout of redundancy – won the grand jury prize at Venice. Telling tales of the disenfranchised is ‘our moral responsibility’, he says. A quintessential 21st-century horror story: a private equity firm has set its sights on your company.
body: In 2009, workers at Ssangyong Motors company protested against plans to lay off between 37 and 43% of the workforce, staging a historic 77-day strike and occupation of the factory that was eventually broken up by riot police. “Until that point in time in Korea, labourers’ rights were widely accepted,” Lee says, speaking through an interpreter in a central London hotel; “however, afterwards, the basic rights of labourers changed; to the public, they couldn’t be seen as more important than market profitability or corporate competitiveness.”

At the time, Lee shelved the project. “The more I examined the pain of these individuals” – after the violent crackdown on the Ssangyong Motors strike, there were several suicides, and reports of long-term mental health issues – “I constantly asked myself: am I worthy of telling this story? And if I am, how do I tell it? Do I stand close to the workers, or keep my distance?” Later he and his co-writer Oh Jung-mi, wrote “many different” scripts, including one with post-apocalyptic elements, before Oh suggested introducing a character who is a documentary film-maker, thereby finding a way to work in Lee’s ambivalence about his intentions.

articles.title: Babydoll singer gives Wales its first UK number one in 15 years
articles.summary: Jamie Miller is the first Welsh artist since 2011 to earn a UK Number 1 single - after Sian Evans' feature on DJ Fresh's Louder.
body: Jamie Miller has become the first Welsh artist to top the UK singles chart in 15 years with his viral TikTok hit, Babydoll.
Miller, who is originally from Pontprennau in Cardiff, narrowly beat Tate McRae and her single Housewife to claim the top spot on the UK Number 1 on Friday, according to the Official Charts Company.
Miller, 29, told Charts: "I don't even know what to say other than thank you so much for getting me Number 1, this is the biggest thing that's ever happened to me in my life, I love you guys."
He is also the first solo male Welsh artist in 41 years to top the singles chart, after Shakin' Stevens' 1985 timeless festive hit, Merry Christmas Everyone.

articles.title: Taika Waititi’s Star Wars film is the latest to hit the buffers. At some point Lucasfilm is going to have to actually make a movie
articles.summary: Waititi joins a long list of movie-makers who were expected to bring a new direction to the franchise, before the studio appeared to get cold feet. Movie-making these days is a very expensive endeavour.
body: Perhaps this is one of the reasons why Disney-owned Lucasfilm seems to be so terrified of making new Star Wars movies. Since 2019’s The Rise of Skywalker, only one Star Wars film, the aforementioned Mando and Grogu movie, has actually made it into cinemas. But that has not stopped the studio announcing a small armada of other projects – sometimes via press release, more often at various high-profile celebrations, conferences or other corporate jamborees – that have so far failed to reach multiplexes.

This week, Taika Waititi revealed in an interview with Inverse that his proposed Star Wars film, announced six years ago, has been “put on ice”. No clear explanation was offered, but frankly nobody should be surprised. It now joins mooted projects from Patty Jenkins, Kevin Feige and Game of Thrones creators David Benioff and DB Weiss on the list of Star Wars movies that we were once told we were definitely (probably) getting, but that we never actually did. Some, such as Rian Johnson’s proposed trilogy, have spent years receding into the distance, while others – Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy’s film about Rey’s new Jedi order, anyone? – have never been officially cancelled.
points: Waititi joins a long list of movie-makers who were expected to bring a new direction to the franchise, before the studio appeared to get cold feet.

articles.title: ‘Overnight, everything was dead’: the Teesside fisherman turned activist dubbed the Mr Bates of the seas
articles.summary: When thousands of dying crabs washed up on a Yorkshire beach in 2021, Stan Rennie’s livelihood was immediately threatened. Five years later, he’s leading the fight back against toxic ocean pollution – and corporate coverups.
body: It was an otherwise typical day on 25 September 2021 when thousands of dead and dying crustaceans washed up on beaches in Yorkshire and the north-east of England. Early morning walkers and swimmers were aghast to find a sickening carpet of twitching, fitting crabs.

It would be the first but not the last die-off, which would see the disappearance of vast swathes of integral native sea life along an extended stretch of coast, including seal pups. It would also see the decimation of the local fishing industry and, with that, a way of life.

Environmentalists, fishers and ordinary local people wondered what could have possibly caused such a rare catastrophic incident. Meanwhile, hours before – completely coincidentally, the authorities said – a major dredging operation was carried out in the mouth of the River Tees, disturbing sediment where decades earlier highly toxic pollutants from heavy industry had been pumped.

The authorities, after carrying out a series of their own tests, denied there was a causal link, blaming an algae bloom and then, later, a novel pathogen. But those who live and work around the Tees estuary disagreed.
points: When thousands of dying crabs washed up on a Yorkshire beach in 2021, Stan Rennie’s livelihood was immediately threatened.
Five years later, he’s leading the fight back against toxic ocean pollution – and corporate coverups.

articles.title: Ethan Klein Says He’s Working to “Urgently Remove My Ownership, Financial Stakes” From H3 Podcast After Wife Hila Klein Reveals His Affair
articles.summary: "We are all shocked, angry, and heartbroken to learn about Ethan’s ongoing affair. As soon as we found out, we all agreed: we would not continue working with Ethan involved or profiting in any way," the crew behind the podcast shared in an Instagram statement.
body: YouTuber Ethan Klein has been dropped from the popular H3 Podcast after his wife Hila Klein revealed that he has been having an affair for over six months, and he’s breaking his silence on the allegations.

The statement continued, “We stand with Hila and will support her every step of the way. We’re disgusted by Ethan’s actions and the hurt he has caused. We all deserved better: Hila, us, and you. “Please know that we’re safe, we’re sticking together, and we’re looking after each other. We’ve put so much of ourselves into this show, and it’s hard to find the words for what we’re feeling right now. Thank you for giving us some time to figure things out, and for all the love you’ve shown us. We love you, and we miss you already.”

Ethan and Hila co-host H3 on their YouTube channel, which has amassed 2.5 million followers. Ethan previously co-hosted the Frenemies podcast (which aired on H3 ‘s YouTube) alongside Trisha Paytas, whom is married to Hila’s brother Moses Hacmon; they canceled that podcast after a fallout.

articles.title: Media Personality Keltie Knight Tapped as Editor-at-Large for Digital Styling App Alta
articles.summary: The Emmy-winner, E! host, 'LadyGang' podcast co-creator and NYT best-selling author will shape Alta's voice across newsletters and social and steer a digital magazine cover set to debut in November.
body: Longtime journalist, host and media personality Keltie Knight will be flexing her Emmy Award winning skills for Alta.

Similar to Cher Horowitz’s desktop styling app featured in Clueless, Alta lets users digitize their wardrobes and receive personalized outfit suggestions based on what they own and customized for weather and whatever is on their calendar for that day. They also get to “try on” those looks via a personal Alta Avatar. Per Alta, more than 700 million outfits have been generated thus far. Alta, which just announced that it had raised $20 million in series A fundraising, has already collaborated with e.l.f. Cosmetics, Gap, Zimmermann, Public School New York and Rent the Runway, and is an official partner of the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA).

“Fashion has always been about the stories we tell with what we wear, and Alta’s community is full of incredible stories,” Knight said in a statement. “I’ve spent my career talking to celebrities on the red carpet. Now I get to celebrate the style of everyone, from the biggest stars to the app users opening their closets on Alta every morning. I can’t wait to show the world what this community is made of.”
